If information is needed on the task's parent job, the dereference parameter may be given a value of 'job'. This will look up the full job document and place it under the 'job' property in the task document. If the output of a child job task is needed, the dereference parameter may be given a value of 'child-job-output'. This will look up the output of the job initiated by the child job task. If the child job has loop settings each individual output will be provided in an array under the property 'variables.outgoing.job_details.loop'. If the child job does not have loop settings, the output of the single job document will be provided under the property 'variables.outgoing.job_details.output'.

Control over the transaction is extended by 30 seconds everytime one of the following is sent-
1. Create/Delete site
2. Add/replace/delete devices from site
3. Sending (this) heartbeat call

name.description: LDAP server name

protocol.description: LDAP server connection Protocol to use

useTrustStore.description: Whether to use certificates stored in NXRM's truststore

port.description: LDAP server connection port to use

searchBase.description: LDAP location to be added to the connection URL

authScheme.description: Authentication scheme used for connecting to LDAP server

authRealm.description: The SASL realm to bind to. Required if authScheme is CRAM_MD5 or DIGEST_MD5

authUsername.description: This must be a fully qualified username if simple authentication is used. Required if authScheme other than none.

connectionTimeoutSeconds.description: How long to wait before timeout

connectionRetryDelaySeconds.description: How long to wait before retrying

userBaseDn.description: The relative DN where user objects are found (e.g. ou=people). This value will have the Search base DN value appended to form the full User search base DN.

userSubtree.description: Are users located in structures below the user base DN?

userLdapFilter.description: LDAP search filter to limit user search

userIdAttribute.description: This is used to find a user given its user ID

userRealNameAttribute.description: This is used to find a real name given the user ID

userEmailAddressAttribute.description: This is used to find an email address given the user ID

userPasswordAttribute.description: If this field is blank the user will be authenticated against a bind with the LDAP server

ldapGroupsAsRoles.description: Denotes whether LDAP assigned roles are used as NXRM roles

groupType.description: Defines a type of groups used: static (a group contains a list of users) or dynamic (a user contains a list of groups). Required if ldapGroupsAsRoles is true.

groupBaseDn.description: The relative DN where group objects are found (e.g. ou=Group). This value will have the Search base DN value appended to form the full Group search base DN.

groupSubtree.description: Are groups located in structures below the group base DN

groupObjectClass.description: LDAP class for group objects. Required if groupType is static

groupIdAttribute.description: This field specifies the attribute of the Object class that defines the Group ID. Required if groupType is static

groupMemberAttribute.description: LDAP attribute containing the usernames for the group. Required if groupType is static

groupMemberFormat.description: The format of user ID stored in the group member attribute. Required if groupType is static

userMemberOfAttribute.description: Set this to the attribute used to store the attribute which holds groups DN in the user object. Required if groupType is dynamic

authPassword.description: The password to bind with. Required if authScheme other than none.

returned will be equivalent to PAGINATE_COUNT. An arbitrary limit (up to MAX_PAGE_SIZE, if set) may be passed,

The advisory lock decorator uses a PostgreSQL advisory lock to prevent this API from being
invoked in parallel, which results in a race condition where multiple insertions can occur.

interface. This is useful in a situation where a device boots with no configuration, but can detect its neighbors

* `peer_interface`: The name of the peer interface

returned will be equivalent to PAGINATE_COUNT. An arbitrary limit (up to MAX_PAGE_SIZE, if set) may be passed,

The advisory lock decorator uses a PostgreSQL advisory lock to prevent this API from being
invoked in parallel, which results in a race condition where multiple insertions can occur.

* `peer_interface`: The name of the peer interface

http_content_type.description: The complete list of official content types is available here.

additional_headers.title: Additional headers
additional_headers.description: User-supplied HTTP headers to be sent with the request in addition to the HTTP content type. Headers should be defined in the format Name: Value. Jinja2 template processing is supported with the same context as the request body (below).

body_template.title: Body template
body_template.description: Jinja2 template for a custom request body. If blank, a JSON object representing the change will be included. Available context data includes: event, model, timestamp, username, request_id, and data.

secret.title: Secret
secret.description: When provided, the request will include a 'X-Hook-Signature' header containing a HMAC hex digest of the payload body using the secret as the key. The secret is not transmitted in the request.

conditions.title: Conditions
conditions.description: A set of conditions which determine whether the webhook will be generated.

ssl_verification.title: SSL verification
ssl_verification.description: Enable SSL certificate verification. Disable with caution!

ca_file_path.title: CA File Path
ca_file_path.description: The specific CA certificate file to use for SSL verification. Leave blank to use the system defaults.

service_management_serviceManagerDoc_ser.title: Service Instance Options
service_management_serviceManagerDoc_ser.description: Optional parameters for testInstances and saveInstances using the new style parameters which support all commit flags. The skip-validation property MUST be included to use this option set. Other properties are optional. With skip-validation, the options object will be parsed and sent to NSO without being validated by the adapter, and the order of the options does matter in several cases.

skip-validation.description: Required to enable commit flag support.

dryrun.description: Use dryrun commit flag. If not dryrun is not set when running testInstances, it will be added with outformat defaulting to native.

reverse.description: Used with native outformat, this flag displays device commands for getting back to current running state in the network if the commit succeeds.

tag.description: User defined opaque tag which is present in all notifications and events sent referencing the specific queue item. This property must be placed first inside the commit-queue property if being used.

sync.description: Uses sync mode for commit queue. Cannot be used with async or bypass mode.

timeout.description: Maximum number of seconds to wait for transaction to be committed.

infinity.description: Use this format for infinite wait time.

async.description: Uses async mode for commit queue. Cannot be used with sync or bypass mode.

bypass.description: Uses bypass mode for commit queue. Cannot be used with sync or async mode.

block-others.description: The commit-queue-block-others flag will block subsequent queue items, which use any of the devices in this queue item, from being queued.

lock.description: The commit-queue-lock flag will place a lock on the resulting queue item.

atomic.description: The commit-queue-atomic sets atomic behavior of resulting queue item.

error-option.description: The commit-queue-error-option flag determines behavior on error.

no-deploy.description: The no-deploy flag makes a commit without invoking the service create method.

no-revision-drop.description: Uses no-revision-drop flag. Forces NSO to not silently drop data set operations.

no-networking.description: The no-networking flag does not send data to the devices.

no-out-of-sync-check.description: The no-out-of-sync-check flag continues with a transaction even when NSO detect an out of sync device. Can't be used with no-overwrite flag.

no-overwrite.description: The no-overwrite flag checks that the data that should be modified has not changed on the device compared to NSO's view of the data. Can't be used with no-out-of-sync-check.

use-lsa.description: The use-lsa flag forces handling of LSA nodes as such. Propogates the following flags, if used, to LSA nodes but not upper NSO node: dry-run, no-networking, no-out-of-sync-check, no-overwrite, no-revision-drop.

no-lsa.description: The no-lsa flag will not handle LSA nodes as such.
